# @k8ordo/form

> Derive HTML constraint attributes, error messages, and server-side validation
> from one zod schema. The DOM holds the values; React state holds only what the
> DOM cannot express. Forms work with JavaScript disabled or not yet loaded.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses only
> what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or legacy
> fallbacks.

When installed via npm, these docs live under `node_modules/@k8ordo/form/docs/`.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](GUIDE.md): the server/client split, writing a form end to end,
  what the package guarantees, what it does not do yet, and how it pairs with
  `@k8ordo/ui` without depending on it.

## Entry points

- `@k8ordo/form` — client. `useForm(fields, state)` takes the whole
  `formFields` result and returns props for the `<form>` element, a
  `field(path)` accessor giving input attributes, the current error, and
  `invalid` / `required`, an `array(path)` accessor for repeated rows, and
  `isDirty`. Also `useAsyncCheck` for server-answered per-field checks and
  `HiddenValue` for components that render no input of their own.
- `@k8ordo/form/server` — server. `formFields(schema)` derives serializable
  fields plus a `dropped` list of checks HTML cannot express, and throws on a
  schema no form can represent; `parseForm(schema, formData)` validates a
  submission and returns typed data or per-field errors with the submitted
  values. `defineForm(schema, rules)` attaches cross-field rules (`sameAs`,
  `minChecked`, `requiredWhen`) typed against the schema's paths.
